_doc: Field-scoped AVAILABILITY evidence, one entry per attributable source per player. Extends the result-evidence discipline. claim is one of confirmed_unavailable | limited_gtd -- nothing else may be asserted. Only an ATTRIBUTABLE PUBLIC source (school_release, school_site, beat_report, broadcast) can support a claim; kind community_forum and cody_observation are SIGNALS -- stored, labelled, and never able to set a status. Every entry carries the exact quoted wording, url, retrieved time, an effective date range and a review_by date; evidence past review_by or outside its effective range supports nothing and the player falls back to the honest default. Support never spills: one entry, one player, one claim, one date range. A DNP row, a zero-action listing, reduced minutes, a roster omission or a social post is NEVER promoted into out/injured/unavailable, and no diagnosis is ever shown unless an official public source used that exact language -- and then only as the source's own quoted words. ADDED 2026-08-30: claim match_incident records a DATED, SOURCED in-match event (left the match, did not return) and sets NO current status -- the player's current availability stays UNKNOWN pending a team update. An incident renders in its own section, never in the sourced-status count. ADDED 2026-09-01: claim out_for_season -- a SOURCED season-ending status (attributable public report with exact wording). Never inferred from an incident; each supporting source is its own entry so attributions stay separate. An entry may carry a short `summary` -- reader-facing wording strictly supported by the quote.

Purdue|Kenna Wollard.quote: Sometimes life changes in ways you could never imagine or prepare for. I'm currently dealing with an unexpected health issue that will keep me away fro a little while. While I'm not ready to share the details at this time, I hope you understand and respect my privacy until I am ready to share more.
Purdue|Kenna Wollard.note: Her own public Instagram statement, reported by Yahoo Sports / Purdue Boilermakers On SI (Dustin Schutte, 2026-08-27). The typo 'fro' is hers and is preserved -- the quote is verbatim. Coach Dave Shondell, same report: "We don't know when for sure she'll be back. That's all I can say." NO diagnosis, hospital, season-ending status or return date is sourced, so none may render. Corroborating participation fact: Creighton's own Aug 28 recap says Purdue 'played without Second Team All-American Kenna Wollard (personal reasons)'.

Purdue|Grace Heaney.note: Purdue's own Aug. 31 match preview ('Big Ten/SEC Challenge Descends on Mackey Arena') states the injury type and the set in its own words -- the school naming a lower-leg injury upgrades the earlier Creighton-recap sourcing. Her CURRENT availability remains UNKNOWN pending a Purdue update: the preview marks Wollard 'out' but assigns Heaney no status.

Texas|Abby Vander Wal.quote: A Monday MRI confirmed the worst fears for Texas volleyball and outside hitter Abby Vander Wal. Vander Wal, a 6-foot-3 starting outside hitter, tore the ACL in her left knee during Saturday's win over TCU and will likely miss the remainder of the season.
Texas|Abby Vander Wal.summary: Left ACL tear reported after Monday MRI
Texas|Abby Vander Wal.note: Austin American-Statesman (Thomas Jones, 2026-08-31), read via its Yahoo syndication. This is a BEAT REPORT of the MRI result -- no Texas Athletics release is held and none is implied. The injury occurred 2026-08-29 v TCU at the Players Era Showcase (Las Vegas).

Texas|Abby Vander Wal.quote: Texas coach Jerritt Elliott said sophomore outside hitter Abby Vander Wal is out for the season with the knee injury that she suffered on Saturday night.
Texas|Abby Vander Wal.summary: Coach-reported: expected to miss the remainder of 2026
Texas|Abby Vander Wal.note: The coach-reported SEASON OUTLOOK, attributed separately from the MRI report: Sports Illustrated / On SI (Paige Durrenberger, 2026-08-30), quoting Lincoln Arneal's report of Jerritt Elliott's statement. Not a Texas Athletics release.
